Thanks for adding a lot of test cases.
The following three constants are already defined in types.hpp. Please use the standard constants.
Done

Done
You could wrap this in std::move() to avoid making a copy.
Done

Done

If I am understanding this correctly, the System class will initialize the chassis containing the BMC to present and all the others to not present.

I don't agree with this. Other firmware (such as VPD collection) may have already set the chassis presence in inventory manager based on GPIOs. So you would be overwriting the correct presence with False. Also, some other applications will take actions based on the value you publish on D-Bus. So we shouldn't publish false if that is not the correct value (haven't read GPIO yet).
Done

The logic here is pretty complex, so I'm not sure I've understood all the cases.

But at a high level, both the PresenceGpio and PresencePath JSON properties are optional. So the user could have specify only the GPIO, only the path, both, or neither.

I'm not sure if all those variations are covered in the if statements below. Also it does not check if presenceGPIOValue has a value. Lastly, this is only called if the GPIO value changes, so if the user had specified only the path then the path presence would be ignored I think?

This story had specifically gone after making changes based on the changed gpio value so I had not put anything in for if there was no presence gpio and there is nothing checking the presence path for changes. The logic in this function covers the presence path not being included. Right now there is no path to get here in the code without the gpio, I can add statements to handle that now or leave it for when a path to this function exists with just the presence path.
Can this method be called before presenceValue has been changed from the initial value of false (from the data member initializer)?
Looking at it again yes, I will change it such that initialize presence will be called before monitor.
If the read failed, why are we logging an error saying the presence was incorrect?
If the read failed it would mean that presence gpios is not matching what it should be (active), and there would be a patch pannel fail.
Why does it matter if the system is powered on? Would probably be worth a comment explaining.
It matters for error logging, we don't want to build up an error log for chassis presence if the system is not on. I will add a comment.
Wouldn't it be better to use the common Services method to log the error here?
I did use servies here?
I think you should put lines 301-303 in the message registry. The callout info could differ across machine types and countries.
I have a story in the backlog to do this, I will remove the callout data here for now.
Same questions as above regarding why a readFailure is handle the same as a 0 value, using Services to log error, why system needs to be powered on, etc.
Done

Once the property has been published on D-Bus, I don't think you need to use Notify to update it. I think you can just set the property. That is probably more efficient. You don't have to build up all those maps and call a more complex API.
That would work. However I'm hesitant because it would require that I need to track weather the property is up on dbus, or have an error handling that can swap the two.

This method is confusing.

I think it would be clearer if the argument was a boolean indicating whether the chassis is initially true or false. If you want the System class to set the chassis containing the BMC to be present, just call initializePresence() on that one chassis.
Done

Nit: If you are trying to refer generally to this application, I think we should remove the hyphens.

The repo name is phosphor-inventory-manager (lower case). The executable is phosphor-inventory.

I agree with referring to it more generally, since the repo or executable name is sort of internal detail that could change.
Done
This will have a default value of false. Is that what you want? Or should it be a std::optional<bool> so the default value is undefined/unknown?
The presence value should be set to true for the chassis with the running bmc, false otherwise. I believe having this default to false is okay.

I don't understand the requirement for this method.

As I mentioned in the chassis class, it is going to set the presence of all the chassis that don't contain the active BMC to false initially. I think this has negative side-effects.

Also, some systems won't have redundant BMCs or the Position property. Won't we get the correct chassis presence from the GPIO and/or path?

We wanted to initialize the chassis with the running bmc to be present and the rest to false. I can make it so that it only runs for the chassis containing the active bmc. Then I can have it such that it will not do anything if there is no position property. We will get the correct presence from the gpio and path, this is purely to set the initial value.

Since the polarity is low, wouldn't values of 1 mean not present? I realize this ends up being a MockGpio, so the polarity is ignored I think. But it makes the test case confusing.

Same question with some of the other test variations.
Because the gpio class handles polarity with the request flags chassis will just see 1 as active(present) and 0 as inactive(not present).
FYI if you don't care about the parameter values you can just omit the entire parenthesized part.
Done

Presence path was not specified vs. not existing, right?

I'm not sure if it affects the code flow, but those are different scenarios.
It does not affect the code flow, but not specified is what happens in this test case
